notesStmt.note: The envelope Whitman used in creating this manuscript is postmarked October 1883, so he must have created this manuscript in late 1883 or early 1884.

"With Husky-Haughty Lips, O Sea!" was published first in the March 1884 issue of Harper's Monthly Magazine. It was reprinted, with the addition of one line, in November Boughs (1888) and in the "Sands at Seventy" annex to Leaves of Grass in 1888 and after.

lg.l: Where day and night I walk thy surf⹀beat shore,
Imaging to my sense thy varied strange suggestions,
Thy troops of white⹀maned racers urging to the goal,

l.add: The ceaseless curious rasping of thy sands and waves,

lg.l: Thy brooding murk and scowl—thy unloos'd hurricanes‸—thy sudden changes

Thy ample smiling face, dash'd with the sparkling
dimples of the sun,

Great as thou art, thy many tears—a lack from
all eternity in thy content,

Thy lonely state—something thou ever seek'st
and seek'st, yet gainest not;
